title: I Am / I Have / I Like / I Want
subtitle: The four sentence patterns that let you say the most, with the least grammar.
objectives: Use "I have" to talk about what you own or your family
Use "I like" to talk about preferences
Use "I want" and "I need" to ask for things

content.intro: You don't need to know all of English grammar to start communicating. These four simple patterns, used correctly, let you say a huge number of useful things right away.

rules.heading: I am + adjective/noun
rules.body: • I am happy. / I am tired. / I am a student.

rules.heading: I have + noun
rules.body: • I have a car. / I have two children. / I have a question.

rules.heading: I like + noun
rules.body: • I like coffee. / I like music. / I like this song.

rules.heading: I want / I need + noun
rules.body: • I want a coffee, please. / I need help. / I need more time.

examples: I want a glass of water, please.
I am a little tired today.

commonMistakes.why: For feelings and descriptions, use "I am," not "I have."

commonMistakes.wrong: I like coffee very much because I want it.
commonMistakes.why: "Like" already expresses that you enjoy something — "want" is for asking for something specific, not needed here.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with am, have, like, or want.

items.explanation: "I have" for what you own or your family.

items.prompt: How do you say you are tired?
How do you ask for water politely?
items.explanation: "I want... please" is the natural way to ask for something.

exercises.title: Practice
exercises.instructions: Write one true sentence about yourself for each pattern.

items.prompt: Write a sentence starting with "I am..."
Write a sentence starting with "I like..."

summary: I have + noun — talk about what you own or your family.
I like + noun — talk about preferences.
I want / I need + noun — ask for something.
